title: Stream protocol handshake, explicit cancel contracts, and resume interop
creator: Sofia Liang
description: Problem: existing Go SDK streaming paths conflate transport-level connection loss with client-initiated cancellation. This leads to surprising behaviors: partial message delivery, KV-cache inconsistencies, and lost resume tokens. Goal: define and implement an explicit handshake and cancel contract for the Go streaming client so callers can distinguish (1) graceful client cancel (intentional abort), (2) transient transport interruption (recoverable), and (3) hard shutdown/server-side cancel (non-recoverable). Deliverables: protocol-level handshake messages, client API ergonomics for context/timeouts, server-side hints for resume eligibility, and end-to-end tests and examples.
acceptance_criteria: API: Go SDK exposes Stream.HandleCancel(ctx) and Stream.Resume(ctx, token) helpers with clear semantics
Behavior: client-initiated cancel results in server receiving an explicit CANCEL intent and avoids creating a resume checkpoint
Behavior: transient transport failure allows automatic reconnect within a configurable window and resume succeeds when server returns a valid resume token
Tests: automated flaky-tolerant integration tests that simulate network partition, client cancel, and server-side abort
Docs: example in sdk/go/examples/stream_resume.md and API docstrings updated
Compatibility: falls back to existing streaming behavior when server does not advertise handshake extension

comments: 2026-03-05 Sofia Liang: Created ticket after observing two production incidents where mobile SDKs reported partial completions and resumed stale KV caches. Root cause traced to ambiguous cancel semantics over streaming transport.
2026-03-07 Sofia Liang: Design review notes - agreed to keep handshake backward compatible by making the server advertise an extension header 'X-Stream-Resume: v1'. If absent clients use legacy flow.

2026-03-09 Ethan Park: Prototype client helpers added. API sketch: Stream.CancelWithIntent(ctx, reason string) and Stream.AttemptResume(ctx) returning (ok bool, err error). Leaving ergonomics open to feedback from DX.
2026-03-10 Daniel Russo (runtime): Server will add two hint fields in control frames: 'resume_token' (opaque) and 'resume_window_ms'. We need to standardize token expiry semantics.
2026-03-11 Priya Menon (QA): Started integration harness for simulated network partitions. Early run shows resume succeeds ~94% of the time; failing cases map to server-side non-resumeable aborts.

2026-03-12 Design review: Agreed to explicit CANCEL vs INTERRUPT semantics. CANCEL == client intent to abort (no resume). INTERRUPT == transient network issue (client should try to reconnect using token).

2026-03-13 Code review: PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/4827 requested to split Stream.Cancel() into CancelIntent() and CancelConnection() to avoid ambiguity. Left TODO to update examples.

2026-03-14 Ethan Park: Wire up context timeout propagation: deadlines set by caller are annotated on handshake frame so runtime can honor early KV cache flushes; added unit tests for context propagation.
test_plan: Unit tests: stream helpers (CancelIntent, CancelConnection, AttemptResume) with fake transport. Integration: cluster CI job that runs a 3-node runtime with chaos monkey toggling TCP connection, validating resume token roundtrip and verifying no duplicate tokens. Load test: bench 1k concurrent short-stream requests and measure added handshake RTT and tail latency. Observability: add metrics stream_handshake_{success,failure}, resume_attempts, resume_success_rate.
notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) Embedding intent in every message vs explicit control frame - chose control frame to minimize payload overhead. (2) Server-issued resume token semantics: opaque vs structured. We keep opaque to avoid tight coupling but add TTL in control frame. (3) Backward compatibility prioritized: handshake is optional and falls back to legacy semantics when absent.
risks: Handshake adds an extra RTT on first message for short-lived streams (mitigation: piggyback handshake on first data frame when possible)
Opaque tokens may require additional server-side state leading to memory pressure (mitigation: token TTL and probabilistic eviction)
Misuse of CancelIntent could be used by clients that expect auto-resume leading to data loss (mitigation: clear docs and API names)
Interoperability gaps between older runtime versions and new handshake spec (mitigation: feature negotiation and logging)
Tests may be flaky under CI due to timing windows; QA to stabilize harness with deterministic network proxies
migration_notes: Existing Go SDK users will keep current behavior. To opt into resume semantics, callers should update to go-sdk-2.4 and adopt Stream.AttemptResume flow. Provide migration snippet in docs that shows how to change Context usage and when to call CancelIntent vs CancelConnection.

estimated_impact: Reduces customer-facing partial-delivery incidents and decreases KV-cache inconsistency regressions under flaky networks. Expected to improve overall stream reliability for mobile and edge clients by ~30% in observed incidents.
